root_motivation: WHO: the agent in its second session that wants to know which of yesterday's six cleaner calls worked, and host.resume, whose session count is a guess. WHAT: host.calls.list rows cannot tell two calls of one tool apart and name no session. WHY: two nullable calls columns, args_sha256 (a masked-arguments fingerprint) and session_id, written by the one writer record_call_traced, let an agent rebuild what a session did without a second reader of the table.
user_persona: An agent (or its operator) who lists its own calls and needs same-tool calls told apart by a fingerprint that never holds a secret value, one session's calls on demand, and a per-session rollup; a tool owner who sees a caller's row with both fields null.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a published tool called with {a:1,b:2}, {b:2,a:1}, {a:1,b:3} and no arguments, When host.calls.list {tool} runs, Then rows 1 and 2 hold one args_sha256, row 3 another and row 4 null, and each non-null value is idempotency::args_sha256 of that call's masked arguments.

Given calls with api_key k-1111 and k-2222 (same q) and a string argument holding an 8-character tenant secret value, When listed, Then the first two share one args_sha256 computed over api_key as ***, the third hashes with the value as {{ secret.NAME }}, and no calls column holds k-1111, k-2222 or the secret value.

Given two MCP sessions on one tenant with 3 and 2 calls of one published tool and one stateless call, When host.calls.list {session, tool} runs for the first id, Then 3 rows return each with that session_id; another tenant's session id returns calls: []; the stateless row reads session_id: null.

Given tenant B calls tenant A's shared tool with arguments over a session, When A runs host.calls.list {credential: shared_caller}, Then that row has null args_sha256 and null session_id; and a host.tool.publish row of A's own made over an MCP session reads null args_sha256 and a non-null session_id.
Given 1000 warm calls with and without the two values written, When record_call_traced's p95 is compared on the gate box, Then the delta is at most 1 ms and both numbers are printed.

Given the two new fields, When the drift tests run, Then CallRow::FIELDS, the fields projection, the host.calls.export CSV header and the contract files from mcphost contract dump list the same fields in the same order, and a source scan finds one INSERT INTO calls that names args_sha256.

Given 3 sessions in one window with 4, 6 and 2 calls (2 failed in the second), When host.calls.sessions runs, Then 3 rows return newest first with those calls counts and failed: 2 on the second, and the verb is in the paged-verb tables and the generated contract (host-tools.v1.json, gendocs).

Given prod after deploy, When tests/jrnl_ac08_live_prod_calls_list_hashes.rs calls one published tool three times with two argument sets over one held Mcp-Session-Id and lists its calls, Then the three rows hold two args_sha256 values and one non-null session_id (Live; evidence: MCPHOST_LIVE=1 MCPHOST_URL=https://mcphost.dev cargo test --test jrnl_ac08_live_prod_calls_list_hashes)
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred: Live (prod; evidence: MCPHOST_LIVE=1 MCPHOST_URL=https://mcphost.dev cargo test --test jrnl_ac08_live_prod_calls_list_hashes)

scope: migrations/0141_calls_args_session.sql; src/db.rs (record_call_traced writes args_sha256 and session_id, migration wiring, calls_dump_for_test); src/calllog.rs (task-locals, CallRow fields, session filter, host.calls.sessions); src/handler.rs (call_tool session scope, call_published_tool fingerprint cell, descriptors); src/handler/arms.rs, src/dispatch_table.rs, src/paged.rs, src/scopes.rs; docs/tools.md, docs/openapi.json, www/llms.txt, contracts/*.json and the SDKs rendered from them.
non_goals: Per-call request and output detail (host.call_trace); error grouping (host.doctor); switching host.resume to session_id; a second cursor, window or list verb; a per-tenant keyed hash; the AC 8 prod read (operator-provisioned, deferred).

additional.no_version_bump: No version file is bumped; wm-build land bumps and tags.
additional.one_writer: record_call_traced's INSERT INTO calls is the only one that writes args_sha256 and session_id; every other insert leaves them NULL.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can an agent not tell its six cleaner calls apart?
five_whys_trace.a: host.calls.list rows differ only in time, outcome and duration; they carry no argument identity.

five_whys_trace.q: Why no argument identity on a row?
five_whys_trace.a: The calls table stores no argument value, deliberately, and no fingerprint of one.

five_whys_trace.q: Why not read the arguments from call_traces?
five_whys_trace.a: A trace is per-call detail with a short retention; a fingerprint on the row lives as long as the row and costs one sha256.
calls has no session column; host.resume guesses sessions from a 30-minute gap.

five_whys_trace.q: Why add columns to the one reader instead of a second journal verb?
five_whys_trace.a: host.calls.list already pages by id with a signed cursor and a retention window; a second reader of calls would duplicate it.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does the first request of a session carry the session id?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No: the host mints the id on that request and the client echoes it from the second on, so a row carries a session_id only when the request presented one; a stateless call reads null.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Which rows leave a host control-plane verb's session visible?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Host verbs write no calls row of their own; the rows that exist (idempotent replays, the progress probe) carry the session id of the request through the call_tool scope and a null args_sha256; a refusal row is written by a separate insert that leaves both columns null.

ambiguities_resolved.question: What do a cross-tenant call's two fields read?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Null: the writer drops both when caller_tenant_id is set, so the owner never sees the caller's session or arguments.
